name: Red nucleus
summary: A large, iron-rich, ovoid nucleus in the midbrain tegmentum at the level of the superior colliculus, pink in fresh specimens and dark on T2-weighted MRI. It receives the crossed outflow of the cerebellar dentate and interposed nuclei through the superior cerebellar peduncle and input from the motor cortex, and it sends the rubrospinal tract (crossed, to flexor motor neurons) and the central tegmental tract (uncrossed, to the inferior olive). The oculomotor fascicles pass straight through it, which is why red nucleus lesions come packaged with a third nerve palsy as the Claude and Benedikt syndromes.

anatomy.location: Central tegmentum of the rostral midbrain, dorsomedial to the substantia nigra and ventrolateral to the periaqueductal gray, extending up into the caudal diencephalon; the two nuclei flank the midline about 6–8 mm apart.

subdivisions.name: Magnocellular part
subdivisions.note: caudal; origin of the rubrospinal tract, small in humans

subdivisions.name: Parvocellular part
subdivisions.note: rostral, the bulk of the nucleus in humans; relays cerebellar and cortical input to the inferior olive through the central tegmental tract

function: Node of the cerebello-rubro-thalamic and rubro-olivary loops that refine limb movement; a minor descending motor pathway (rubrospinal) favoring upper limb flexors, which becomes relevant in decorticate posturing.

bestView.label: paired dark round nuclei in the midbrain tegmentum at the superior colliculus level
red nuclei above the substantia nigra

imaging.normalAppearance: Distinctly dark round nuclei on T2 and SWI because of iron, easily identified on axial slices through the upper midbrain behind the substantia nigra; on T1 they are nearly isointense.

pathology.finding: Paramedian midbrain tegmental restricted diffusion involving the red nucleus and the adjacent oculomotor fascicles.
Lesion (infarct, hemorrhage, demyelination) of the red nucleus region or the dentatorubrothalamic fibers, appearing weeks to months before a slow rest-postural-intention tremor.
pathology.timing: Tremor emerges 1–24 months after the lesion

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Axial DWI and T2/SWI through the midbrain

lesionEffects.mechanism: Crossed dentatothalamic fibers passing through and around the nucleus

lesionEffects.deficit: Contralateral coarse tremor, chorea and athetosis (Benedikt)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Red nucleus plus the adjacent substantia nigra and cerebellothalamic fibers
Lesions above the red nucleus leave the rubrospinal flexor drive to the arms unopposed

examination: Finger-nose for terminal tremor and past-pointing
Observe the arm at rest, with posture and with action for a Holmes tremor
pearls: Third nerve palsy plus contralateral tremor or ataxia localizes to the red nucleus region
Decorticate posture means the lesion is above the red nucleus; decerebrate posture means it is below
